overview: A one-page Department of State list-of-papers sheet for file 894C.74, concerning wireless telegraphy in the Kwantung Leased Territory. It indexes an April 27, 1936 report from Grummon at Dairen about military-police surveillance of shortwave radios: the local RCA Victor manager had reportedly been ordered to disclose all sales of shortwave sets to Dairen dealers, potentially affecting American business interests.

people.name: Philip D. Grummon
people.role: Official reporting from Dairen; precise position is not stated on the sheet

subfiles.title: List of Papers: Surveillance of Shortwave Radio Sales in Dairen
subfiles.from: Department of State, indexing a report from Grummon at Dairen
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes a report that military police required the Dairen manager of the RCA Victor Company to identify sales of shortwave radio sets to local dealers.
subfiles.summary: This Department of State filing sheet records one paper dated April 27, 1936, sent from Dairen by Grummon to “FE.” According to its précis, the Dairen manager of the RCA Victor Company had been asked to furnish the military police with a list of all shortwave-radio sales to the company’s local dealers. The indexed report addressed the consequences of this surveillance for American business.

interest: The sheet is useful as evidence of Japanese military-police monitoring of communications technology and its intersection with foreign commerce in Dairen during 1936. Although the underlying report is absent, the précis preserves its central allegation and identifies its date, origin, author, and departmental destination. It also illustrates how the State Department classified commercial concerns about radio surveillance under wireless telegraphy for the Kwantung Leased Territory.
